Counsel,

edits.text: 2. CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION. “Confidential Information” means any non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of a party or its affiliates (the “Disclosing Party”) to the other party or its affiliates or representatives (the “Receiving Party”), whether before or after the date of this Agreement, in oral, written, electronic, visual, or other form, that is identified as confidential or proprietary or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Confidential Information includes analyses, notes, summaries, compilations, and other materials prepared by the Receiving Party or its representatives that contain or reflect Confidential Information. “Representatives” means a party’s and its affiliates’ directors, officers, employees, partners, members, managers, agents, advisors, attorneys, accountants, consultants, financing sources, and other representatives.
edits.name: Replace Section 2 heading and add definition

edits.text: 3. CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS. Each Receiving Party shall use the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information solely to evaluate, negotiate, and, if applicable, consummate the potential transaction between the parties (the “Purpose”) and shall not disclose Confidential Information except to its affiliates and Representatives who have a need to know for the Purpose and are informed of the confidential nature of the information or are otherwise bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective in all material respects than those set forth in this Agreement. The Receiving Party shall protect Confidential Information from unauthorized use or disclosure using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature, and in no event less than reasonable care, and shall be responsible for any breach of this Agreement by its affiliates or Representatives.
edits.name: Replace former Term with confidentiality obligations / permitted recipients

edits.text: 4. EXCLUSIONS. Confidential Information does not include information that the Receiving Party can demonstrate: (a) is or becomes publicly available other than as a result of a breach of this Agreement by the Receiving Party or its affiliates or Representatives; (b) was lawfully known to the Receiving Party before disclosure by the Disclosing Party without any obligation of confidentiality; (c) is lawfully received by the Receiving Party from a third party without, to the Receiving Party’s knowledge, breach of any obligation of confidentiality; or (d) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information.
edits.name: Replace former Remedies with exclusions

edits.text: 5. COMPELLED DISCLOSURE. If the Receiving Party or any of its affiliates or Representatives is required by law, regulation, court order, subpoena, or other legal or governmental process to disclose any Confidential Information, the Receiving Party shall, to the extent legally permitted, promptly notify the Disclosing Party and reasonably cooperate with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party’s expense, in seeking confidential treatment, a protective order, or other appropriate remedy. If disclosure is nevertheless required, the Receiving Party may disclose only the portion of Confidential Information that it is legally required to disclose and shall use reasonable efforts to obtain confidential treatment for the disclosed information.
edits.name: Add compelled disclosure

edits.text: 6. RETURN OR DESTRUCTION. Upon the Disclosing Party’s written request, the Receiving Party shall promptly return or destroy the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information in its possession or control, including materials prepared by the Receiving Party or its Representatives that contain or reflect such Confidential Information, and upon request certify such return or destruction. The Receiving Party may retain one archival copy solely for legal, compliance, or record-retention purposes, and may retain copies maintained in routine backup or disaster-recovery systems, provided that retained information remains subject to this Agreement for so long as retained.
edits.name: Add return/destruction

edits.text: 7. NO LICENSE; NO OBLIGATION. All Confidential Information remains the property of the Disclosing Party. No license or other rights, by implication, estoppel, or otherwise, are granted under any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, or other intellectual property or proprietary rights by the disclosure of Confidential Information. Neither party is obligated to proceed with any transaction or business relationship, and either party may terminate discussions at any time in its sole discretion.
edits.name: Add no license / no obligation

edits.text: 8. TERM; SURVIVAL. This Agreement remains in effect for twenty-four months from the date of signing; provided that each party’s obligations with respect to Confidential Information disclosed during the term shall survive for five years from the date of disclosure, except that Confidential Information constituting a trade secret shall remain protected for so long as it qualifies as a trade secret under applicable law.
edits.name: Add revised term/survival

edits.text: 9. REMEDIES. Each party acknowledges that unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages may be inadequate. Accordingly, the Disclosing Party may seek injunctive or equitable relief, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity.
edits.name: Renumber remedies
